Œuvres du domaine public au Met (Open Access, CC0), aucune déjà postée ce mois-ci. Faits vérifiés : Degas, Femme assise à côté d'un vase de fleurs (signé 1865) : peut-être Madame Paul Valpinçon (notice du Met). Van Gogh, Souliers (1888) : peint à Arles, sol carrelé ; plusieurs toiles de chaussures (Paris 1886-87, Arles 1888). Sisley, Rue Eugène Moussoir à Moret, l'hiver (1891) : Moret-sur-Loing, où Sisley vit ses dernières années. Leighton, Lachrymae (1894-95) : « larmes » en latin ; nommé baron le 24 janvier 1896, mort le 25 janvier 1896. Slide Artura : version `cta C`, son logo sous le paragraphe, jamais une capture. Couverture : une vraie photo de musée de la banque de l'OS (id dans `banque`), jamais d'image IA.

en.titre: Paintings That Feel Like Being Alone
A Woman Seated beside a Vase of Flowers
en.texte: pushes its sitter to the very edge, while a huge bouquet takes the center. She looks away from everything, lost in thought. Degas signed it in 1865, and it may show Madame Valpinçon, the wife of a close friend.
was painted in Arles in 1888: just a pair of worn boots on a tiled floor. Van Gogh painted shoes again and again, as if they could tell the story of the people who walked in them.

en.titre: Rue Eugène Moussoir at Moret: Winter
en.texte: is an almost empty street in the small town where Sisley lived his last years. He painted it under snow in 1891, with only a few tiny figures walking away.

means tears. A woman in black leans against a column beside a tomb, holding a wreath. Leighton painted it in his last years; he died in 1896, the day after he was made a lord. Artura gives me one painting a day and the story behind it; this one stayed with me.
